clearedSpotChecks.check: ruint fixes after the pinned versions (1.20.0 on Celo, 1.18.0 on X Layer): PR 603 and PR 666, with the claim that the SHL, SHR and SAR handlers of both images test the whole amount word before shifting.
clearedSpotChecks.note: The result holds on both endpoints. I ran 144 eth_call cases per endpoint (SHL, SHR and SAR on four values, including 2^256-1 and words with the sign bit set, and twelve amounts: 2^32, 2^32+1, 2^32+255, 2^64+1, 2^64+200, 2^128+1, 2^160+3, 2^192+1, 2^255, 2^256-1, 255 and 256). Every case on https://forno.celo.org (reth/v2.2.0-74cc8bb) and https://rpc.xlayer.tech (reth/v2.3.0-f60420a/xlayer/v0.0.7) returned the specified word, with 0 mismatches. The fetched ruint CHANGELOG.md describes PR 603 in other terms than the research file does. It says the PR fixes overflow-flag false negatives in overflowing_shl and overflowing_shr, which also corrected the dependent checked, strict and saturating shifts and byte(). It does not mention a u32 cast in the LIMBS 1, 2 and 4 fast paths. I could not open the PR page (https://github.com/alloy-rs/ruint/pull/603 is not reachable from this session), so the research file's wording of the PR is unconfirmed. The changelog names byte(), and ruint 1.18.0 on X Layer predates the fix, so I also ran BYTE with 49 indices (0 to 39, 2^32, 2^32+1, 2^32+31, 2^64+1, 2^64+31, 2^128+5, 2^255+3, 7*2^64+2 and 2^256-1) on two values. All 98 cases matched on both endpoints. The changelog says PR 666 changes div_3x2_ref, which matches the research file. The shift amounts in src are constants below 256 (TickMath.sol:63, :111; TickBitmap.sol:38), so the PoolManager does not shift by a large amount in any case. The clearance stands.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Arithmetic, comparison and shift handlers of the shipped celo-reth v1.0.10 and xlayer-reth v0.0.7.3-rc.1 images run in the x86-64 model on the inputs that decide FullMath, TickMath, BitMath and TickBitmap.
clearedSpotChecks.note: The stored outputs match the claim. The three Celo shards arith-celo-a-0.json to -2.json hold 107,999 cases each, 323,997 in total, with 0 mismatches and 0 errors. The four X Layer shards hold 323,997 cases with 0 mismatches and 7,405 errors, all SIGNEXTEND. The SIGNEXTEND rerun arith-xl-a-sx.json holds 11,785 cases with 0 mismatches and 0 errors. The planted SHL bound fault on Celo gave 20 mismatches in 4,817 cases, so the harness detects a wrong handler. I did not repeat the emulator runs. This clearance rests on a model of the binaries, not on the nodes as they run. The on-chain battery and the shift and BYTE cases I ran on both endpoints back it at the RPC level.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Legacy jump destination analysis of both images on the PoolManager runtime and 509 other programs, as it decides which JUMP and JUMPI targets of the PoolManager are valid.
clearedSpotChecks.note: jd-celo.json and jd-xl.json each record 510 cases with 0 mismatches. They also record 610 accepted JUMPDEST in the 24,009 byte PoolManager runtime, equal to the specification, with 29 0x5b bytes inside push data excluded. I ran four eth_call programs on each endpoint. A jump to a JUMPDEST at offset 3 returned 1. A jump into a 0x5b inside PUSH1 data was refused with InvalidJump. A jump to a STOP byte was refused with InvalidJump. A jump to a valid JUMPDEST followed by a second JUMP on an empty stack gave StackUnderflow. All four results follow the specification on both chains. In one run before this set, forno answered a malformed probe with the geth-style message invalid jump destination. That fits the mixed op-geth backend already recorded in F-116; the outcome was the same.
